newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Ramos issued tough orders to the National Bureau of Investigation and the Philippine National Police to catch fugitive Congressman Romeo Jalosjos and put him behind bars. (ALL NEWSPAERS)

- The Palace chided the winner in the failed bidding for the Subic container port concession, saying Hutchison Ports Philippines Inc should participate in the re-bidding ordered by President Ramos. (STAR)
- The 1997 budget will likely be approved before Congress resumes session on January 20 after lawmakers agreed to keep the Countrywide Development Fund intact. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Stable supply of rice and corn pushed down the average inflation rate in 1996 to 8.4 percent after hitting double-digit figures in late 1995 and early 1996, the National Statistics Office reported. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Central Bank will sign a U.S. dollar repurchase agreement with the Bank of China, Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson announced. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System accepted sealed bids from four groups vying for the right to operate and manage the state-owned waterworks system. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
